changes.catalogueSays: civil-code 176 يحكم على المدين بتعويض الضرر الناجم عن عدم التنفيذ أو التأخر فيه
changes.reason: [civil-code 176 ¶1] orders the debtor to compensate non-performance and delay, as the catalogue says; the same paragraph adds the debtor's release when he proves a cause beyond his control, which the statement now states. No final module item rests on it, so it stays the claim's own required basis.

changes.catalogueSays: civil-code 179 لا يستحق التعويض إلا بعد إعذار المدين
changes.reason: [civil-code 179 ¶1] makes compensation due only after notice, unless a text provides otherwise; the formal-notice module carries this statement and the prior step resting on it, so both are imported.

changes.catalogueSays: civil-code 182 تقدير التعويض: ما لحق من خسارة وما فات من كسب
changes.reason: [civil-code 182 ¶1] has the judge assess loss suffered and profit lost as the natural result of the breach; [civil-code 182 ¶2], added as its own statement, limits contractual damages to foreseeable damage absent fraud or gross fault.

[civil-code 107 ¶1] requires performance according to the terms and in good faith; [civil-code 107 ¶2] (the contract's necessary incidents) and [civil-code 107 ¶3] (unforeseen events, a defence) are added as their own statements.
[civil-code 106 ¶1] states the binding force of the contract; the formal-notice module carries it and its boundary n10 rests on it, so the statement is imported, not restated.

changes.catalogueSays: إلزام المدعى عليه بأن يؤدي للمدعي تعويضا قدره (...) دج جبرا للضرر اللاحق به
changes.reason: [civil-code 176 ¶1] grounds the award and [civil-code 182 ¶1] its measure; the line now names the breached obligation.
[cpca 419 ¶1] puts the costs on the losing party unless the judge, giving reasons, decides otherwise.

[civil-code 323 ¶1] puts the proof of the obligation on the creditor, and [civil-code 333 ¶1] bars proof by witnesses above the fixed sum outside commercial matters, where [commercial-code 30 ¶7] allows any means.
[civil-code 182 ¶1] measures compensation by the loss suffered and the profit lost, which the plaintiff must show.

[civil-code 180 ¶1] allows notice by warning, an equivalent act, post or an agreed default clause, and [civil-code 181 ¶1] lists cases with no notice; a bailiff's record is therefore not always the document, so the module's documents, each required only in its case, are imported.
[civil-code 323 ¶1] puts the proof of the obligation on the creditor; element e1 states the contract and the obligation agreed.
[civil-code 176 ¶1] awards damages for non-performance or delay; element e2 carries the four kinds of breach of the brief.
[civil-code 182 ¶1] and [civil-code 182 ¶2]: loss and lost profit, foreseeable at contracting unless fraud or gross fault.
[civil-code 182 ¶1] requires the damage to be the natural result of the breach, one the creditor could not avoid by reasonable effort; [civil-code 177 ¶1] reduces it for the creditor's own fault.

changes.catalogueSays: لا يستحق التعويض إلا بعد إعذار المدين
changes.reason: [civil-code 179 ¶1] makes notice a condition of compensation; the formal-notice prior step p1 carries it with the exemptions of [civil-code 181 ¶2] to [civil-code 181 ¶5], and element e5 states the fact to prove.
[civil-code 179 ¶1]: the notice, or its exemption, is a fact the plaintiff states; the brief's element notice_served is carried here.
[civil-code 366 ¶1] time-bars the buyer's claims for a short quantity one year after actual delivery; whether it reaches damages is a reading, so the item warns.

[civil-code 383 ¶1] time-bars the warranty claim one year after delivery, and [civil-code 383 ¶2] lifts it for fraudulent concealment; whether it governs damages for a defect is a reading, so the item warns.
[civil-code 557 ¶1] time-bars the warranty claims against architect and contractor three years after the collapse or discovery of the defect; a limitation warns.

[civil-code 308 ¶1] sets the general limitation and [civil-code 315 ¶1] runs it from the due date; [civil-code 314 ¶1] and [civil-code 3 ¶1] count it, and [civil-code 321 ¶1] forbids the court to raise it of its own motion.

[civil-code 180 ¶1] sets the means of notice and [civil-code 181 ¶1] its exemptions; [civil-code 164 ¶1] requires notice before performance in kind, [civil-code 183 ¶1] applies these rules to agreed damages and [civil-code 186 ¶1] governs delay in paying money.
[cpca 32 ¶4] lists cases before the sections by the nature of the dispute and [cpca 32 ¶5] leaves every non-social dispute to the civil section in a court without sections.

[cpca 37 ¶1] gives the court of the defendant's domicile, [cpca 39 ¶1] opens the list of special venues, among them supplies, works and commercial matters, and [cpca 45 ¶1] voids a jurisdiction clause except between traders.

[cpca 800 ¶2] sends claims with a public administrative party to the administrative courts, [cpca 536 مكرر ¶1] gives listed matters to the specialised commercial court, and [civil-code 339 ¶1] ties the civil judge to a criminal judgment.

[cpca 536 مكرر 4 ¶1] puts a conciliation before a claim at the specialised commercial court, and the module reads its third paragraph as requiring the record of non-conciliation on pain of inadmissibility.
[cpca 17 ¶3] requires a petition about a published property or real right to be published at the land registry.
[cpca 15 ¶1] lists the petition's mandatory particulars on pain of formal inadmissibility, and [cpca 13 ¶1] requires standing and interest.
[civil-code 176 ¶1] grounds damages with the contract kept alive; a rescission request is another claim.
[civil-code 186 ¶1] gives delay in paying a sum of money between individuals its own rule.
[civil-code 182 ¶2] confines its foreseeability limit to obligations arising from a contract; harm from a harmful act is another claim.
[cpca 500 ¶3] gives the social section exclusive jurisdiction over the performance and termination of employment contracts.
[civil-code 107 ¶3] lets the judge reduce an obligation made onerous by unforeseen events, a defence the lawyer should expect.
[civil-code 184 ¶1], [civil-code 184 ¶2] and [civil-code 185 ¶1] govern agreed damages: not due without damage, reducible, and exceeded only for fraud or gross fault.
[civil-code 178 ¶2] allows clauses exempting contractual liability except for the debtor's fraud or gross fault.
The carriage provisions are not in the store; [commercial-code 30 ¶1] is the only commercial contract text found, so the boundary warns to check them (open point o1).
The commercial-lease regime of the Commercial Code is a separate module with no final record; the boundary warns when the lease is commercial, beside the section rule of [cpca 32 ¶4].
[civil-code 379 ¶1] makes the seller answer for defects and promised qualities, with its own period in [civil-code 383 ¶1].
[civil-code 554 ¶1] sets the joint guarantee of architect and contractor, running from final acceptance under [civil-code 554 ¶2], with its own period in [civil-code 557 ¶1].
[civil-code 170 ¶1] lets the creditor have an obligation to act performed at the debtor's expense; performance is the brief's request kind other.
[civil-code 174 ¶1] allows a penalty payment to compel personal performance, and [civil-code 175 ¶1] fixes the final compensation.
[cpca 323 ¶2] orders provisional execution on request for a judgment resting on an official deed or acknowledged promise, and [cpca 323 ¶3] allows it in urgency otherwise.

[civil-code 177 ¶1] (creditor's fault), [civil-code 182 مكرر ¶1] (moral damage), [civil-code 172 ¶1] and [civil-code 172 ¶2] (obligations of care), [civil-code 364 ¶1] and [civil-code 365 ¶1] (seller's duty to deliver) support the elements.
[civil-code 323 ¶1], [civil-code 333 ¶1] and [commercial-code 30 ¶7] set who proves and how; the proof module has no final record to import.
[civil-code 176 ¶1] calls for proof of the breach; [civil-code 366 ¶1], [civil-code 383 ¶1] and [civil-code 557 ¶1] start their periods from dates these documents prove.
